papers.title: Local cohomology over Steenrod algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q = p^s$ elements. Let $S = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} S_n$ be a non-negatively graded commutative, Noetherian $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra. Assume $S$ has a structure of an unstable Steenrod algebra. Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded unstable $S$-module. Let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal in $S$. We prove that for $i \geq 0$ the local cohomology modules $H^i_I(M)$ has a structure of a Cartan $S$-module. As application we give a direct and considerably simpler proof of D. Bourguiba and S. Zarati's generalization of Landweber-Stong conjecture. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for $S$ to have $S_r$-property of Serre in terms of Dickson polynomials.

papers.title: Uniform and Relative Non-Associativity on Minimal Free Resolutions
papers.abstract: We study unital chain-map multiplications on minimal free resolutions of quotient rings. We prove that Katth\"an's example admits no associative multiplication over any field, without assuming graded commutativity or compatibility with an internal grading. The proof gives a relative obstruction in which associativity on a specified finite collection of triples forces failure at another triple. The argument extends to a family that includes nonmonomial ideals. We also give criteria for uniform non-associativity, where a fixed triple fails for every multiplication, by comparing either associators or their primitives under changes of multiplication. These criteria persist from monomial elimination ideals and give explicit obstructions for Avramov's example and the known eight-vertex Bier sphere over every field. As an application, we show that the edge ideal of the eight-cycle admits an injective Taylor comparison on five selected generators, while every selection of that size fails to admit a multiplicative comparison. Four generators admit a multiplicative embedding.

papers.title: Pruning free resolutions over a complete intersection
papers.abstract: Given a free resolution $F_\bullet$ over a polynomial ring $R$ and a system of higher homotopies on it for a regular sequence $a_1,\dots,a_c$, we can use the Eisenbud-Shamash construction to build a free resolution over $\overline{R}=R/(a_1,\dots,a_c)$. We provide a combinatorial formula for the new system of higher homotopies on a pruned free resolution $F_{\bullet}^{\mathcal{M}}$ that corresponds to a pruning of the Eisenbud-Shamash resolution.

papers.title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.

papers.title: The Woo-Yong conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Woo-Yong conjecture: the non-Gorenstein locus of a type A Schubert variety is the union of its generically non-Gorenstein maximal singular components. More strongly, at every scheme point, local Weil divisor classes are detected at the generic points of the maximal singular components containing that point. For arbitrary finite crystallographic type, the analogous localization map is injective on the torsion subgroup of the source local class group. This determines Cartier indices of locally $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisors and gives the Woo-Yong criterion on the $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein locus. A type D family shows the necessity of this hypothesis: the ambient variety is generically Gorenstein along its singular locus but not $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein along a deeper nonempty locus. The type A proof and the counterexamples are geometric; the general torsion proof also uses bounded finite inputs with explicit certificates and reproducible reconstruction programs.

papers.title: The covariety of numerical semigroups with some prescribed pseudo-Frobenius numbers
papers.abstract: If $S$ is a numerical semigroup, then we denote by $m(S)$, $F(S)$ and $\mathrm{PF}(S)$ its multiplicity, its Frobenius number and its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, respectively. Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of positive integers. In this paper, we prove that $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{S\mid F(S)=\max(\mathcal P),\ \mathcal P\subseteq\mathrm{PF}(S)\}$ is a covariety. The associated tree provides algorithms to compute $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, its elements with a prescribed type or genus, and the set of numerical semigroups $S$ satisfying $\mathrm{PF}(S)=\mathcal P$. We show that every element of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ has a unique minimal system of generators relative to $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, and we call its cardinality the $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank. Finally, we characterize the elements of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ with $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank one.

papers.title: A generalized Saito criterion, from line arrangements to curves
papers.abstract: We formulate a generalized Saito criterion for complex projective plane curves, building on a recent generalized Saito criterion for plus-one generated arrangements of hyperplanes due to Junyan Chu.

papers.title: Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals
papers.abstract: We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations. We prove that, under these bounds, an intersection of $T$-ideals is contained in such a product only if one member is. This proves Berele's Conjecture~3 and, consequently, his Conjecture~1 \cite{Berele2012}. We also characterize inclusions between ordered products by an explicit combinatorial criterion, proving his Conjecture~2 and answering his Question~2 \cite{Berele2012}. These results characterize inclusions between arbitrary intersections of products of nonzero proper verbally prime $T$-ideals and show that every nonzero such intersection has a unique finite irredundant representation. As an application, we characterize finite quivers whose path algebras have the same polynomial identities as some, equivalently every, positive power of their arrow ideals.

papers.title: On local cohomology modules over ramified regular local rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show examples of local cohomology modules over ramified regular local ring, having finite set of associated primes. In doing so we consider our ramified regular local ring as Eisenstein extension of an unramified regular local ring sitting inside it. In ramified regular local ring for extended ideal (from the unramified one) set of associated primes of a local cohomology module is always finite. Using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, we construct examples of local cohomology of non extended ideal, whose set of associated primes is finite. In particular, we choose those non extended ideals whose minimal primes are extended ideals which are all cohomologically complete intersection.

papers.title: Generalised Buchberger and Schreyer algorithms for strongly discrete coherent rings
papers.abstract: Let M be a finitely generated submodule of a free module over a multivariate polynomial ring with coefficients in a discrete coherent ring. We prove that its module MLT(M) of leading terms is countably generated and give an algorithm for computing explicitly a generating set. This result is also useful when MLT(M) is not finitely generated. Suppose that the base ring is strongly discrete coherent. We provide a Buchberger-like algorithm and prove that it converges if and only if the module of leading terms is finitely generated. We also state a constructive version of Hilbert's syzygy theorem by following Schreyer's method.

papers.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Br\"and\'en and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

papers.title: Quasihomogeneous isolated singularities in terms of syzygies and foliations
papers.abstract: One considers quasihomogeneous isolated singularities of hypersurfaces in arbitrary dimensions through the lenses of three apparently quite apart themes: syzygies, singularity invariants, and foliations. In the first of these, one adds to the well-known result of Saito a syzygy-theoretic characterization of a quasihomogeneous singularity affording an effective computational criterion. In the second theme, one explores the Milnor-Tjurina difference number from a commutative algebra viewpoint. Building on the Briancon-Skoda theorem and exponent, we extend previously known inequalities by Dimca and Greuel to arbitrary dimension and provide algebraic formulas involving the syzygy-theoretic part and reduction exponents. In the last theme, one recovers and brings to algebraic light a result of Camacho and Movasati by establishing a couple of characterizations of quasihomogeneous isolated singularities in terms of the generators of the module of invariant vector fields.

papers.title: Topological insights into Monoids and Module systems
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a monoid and let $G$ denote its quotient groupoid. We introduce the Riemann-Zariski space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ associated with $H$ and prove that it is a spectral space. We then show that, if $H$ is an $s$-Pr\"ufer monoid, the space $\textup{Zar}(G| H)$ is homeomorphic to the prime $s$-spectrum of $H$ endowed with the Zariski topology. Next, given a finitary ideal system $r$ on $H$, we prove that the space of $r$-ideals $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$, endowed with the Zariski topology, is spectral, and that the prime $r$-spectrum of $H$ is proconstructible in $\mathcal{I}_r(H)$. We also introduce a new topology on the set $\mathcal{X}$ of all generalized $H$-module systems and study its properties. In particular, we show that $\mathcal{X}$ and its subspace $\mathcal{X}_{\textup{fin}}$ of finitary generalized $H$-module systems are spectral spaces. Finally, we provide a characterization of those subsets of the set of overmonoids of $H$ that are quasi-compact.
